newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Telstra wants assistance charges.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Telstra wants assistance charges.

text.p: Australia's government-owned telecoms carrier Telstra Corp said it proposed a A$50 million package of price reductions, incorporating a 50 cent charge for some directory assistance services.

Telstra's National General Manager, Operator Services, Andrew Day said it was considering reducing every customer's fixed telephone line rental by A$5 a year if it charged for some directory assistance services.
Day said the plan could include enhanced directory services at reduced prices.
"Only requests for numbers that are already listed in the local White Pages directory will cost 50 cents," Day said in a statement.
"The service now takes about 8.5 million calls every week and this is growing at a rapid and unsustainable rate of up to 25 percent a year," he said.
At this stage it was an informal proposal and Telstra would discuss it with consumer groups before presenting a formal plan to the government, he said.
The government said during the March 1996 election campaign that it was opposed to charges being levied on Telstra's directory assistance services.
It also plans to sell one-third of Telstra during the life of the current Parliament, raising about A$8 billion.
